authority_rule: This file is the sole authoritative project-management decision source. Other docs/data may describe implementation details but must not override requirements, priorities, decisions, conflicts, active gate, or quality status recorded here.
product_north_star: Let the player live the Peter Jackson film story as a playable adventure rather than inventing a replacement main story.
Make the world feel alive, beautiful, explorable and responsive while preserving story chronology and low-spec performance.
Preserve every meaningful user request and decision so chat loss or developer changes never erase project intent.
Prefer player enjoyment, clarity, stable traversal, save continuity and reliable performance over uncontrolled feature quantity.
operating_rules: Global project-management changes go through the single Governor and a validation branch/PR; workers must not create competing authority files.
One governor, one decision authority. No secondary file may independently redefine requirement status, priority, conflict resolution, active gate, or region acceptance.
Every meaningful user request receives a stable requirement ID here before or with implementation.
New requests never silently delete older requests; contradictions become explicit conflicts/decisions here.
The film story spine, build/save/story integrity, target-device performance and required traversal cannot be silently traded away.
A feature is never called accepted from compile/static evidence alone.
If a previously passed critical gate fails, stop feature expansion, repair the smallest failing layer, and rerun the exact failed gate.
Human pacing and visual review are mandatory for enjoyment/acceptance; CI cannot infer fun.

hard_invariants.description: Meaningful user requirements and decisions must be persisted in repository data; chat history is never the sole source of truth.
Peter Jackson film continuity remains the primary story spine unless the user explicitly records a product-direction override.
A change must not knowingly introduce build failure, crash, save corruption, story deadlock or route-state loss.
Intended playable routes and required story anchors must not be accepted while blocked, trapping the player, or unreachable.
Features must remain compatible with the target laptop profile: Windows DX11, 720p, Low/Medium, 30 FPS floor target, 8 GB RAM, roughly 2 GB VRAM-class GPU.
Static/compile success must never be presented as PIE, device, performance, pacing or visual acceptance.

conflict_rules: A new request never silently deletes or rewrites an older requirement.
If two active requirements conflict, the conflict must be explicitly recorded and resolved before either can be treated as fully accepted.
Hard invariants cannot be silently overridden by implementation convenience.
A user may explicitly change product direction; that override must be recorded as a decision and linked to affected requirements.
When no explicit user override exists, prefer preserving story/progress integrity and target-device playability over visual scope or feature quantity.
Prefer the smallest change that satisfies the request without destabilizing already validated behavior.

decisions.title: Film story anchors versus player exploration freedom
decisions.resolution: Major film chronology/outcomes remain fixed; exploration, side routes, optional conversations and living-world activity belong primarily between required story anchors.
decisions.rationale: Preserves the user's goal of living the film while allowing meaningful adventure and discovery.

decisions.title: Living-world richness versus target-laptop performance
decisions.resolution: Use rich near-player simulation and cheaper distance-adaptive/offscreen simulation; do not require always-on expensive AI for ambient life.
decisions.rationale: The world should feel alive without sacrificing the low-spec device target.

decisions.title: Source reorganization versus current functional validation gate
decisions.resolution: Define and guard the target Public/Private source architecture now, but perform the physical move as a dedicated maintenance pass after the current F9/F8/chapter/device functional gate is healthy.
decisions.rationale: Preserves organization without mixing a large path/include refactor into unresolved gameplay validation.

decisions.title: Begin a bounded visible character-production pass before the full functional hard gate is manually closed
decisions.resolution: Proceed with a small reversible Frodo/Gandalf visual-motion pass now because the user explicitly wants the game to start feeling playable. Do not change story/save architecture or add a large new subsystem; require static and UE4.27.2 build validation, then return to PIE/device gate evidence.
decisions.rationale: This satisfies the user's explicit current direction while limiting regression risk and preserving the existing hard-gate discipline.

decisions.title: Expand visible character production from player avatars to the full Part I core cast
decisions.resolution: Populate each Part I chapter with its required named cast and regional inhabitants now, while keeping expensive simulation near-player only and preserving film chronology. Use distinct proxies where dedicated production assets do not yet exist, and track those proxies as unfinished rather than pretending the cast is visually complete.
decisions.rationale: The user explicitly wants the world to start feeling inhabited and playable now; chapter-appropriate cast presence gives immediate experiential value without waiting for every final character asset.

decisions.title: Build first in larger batches, then perform a dedicated integration/playtest repair pass
decisions.resolution: Continue substantial character/world/runtime construction now while requiring Pre-Unreal and real UE4.27.2 compile/import gates for each merged batch. Defer detailed PIE, device, pacing and visual acceptance into a later dedicated integration/playtest/repair pass instead of stopping after every small visible feature.
decisions.rationale: The user explicitly wants to see a much more complete game when returning to the laptop and prefers building a larger playable body of work before manual testing.

update_protocol: Treat Data/ProjectGovernor.json as the first-read/last-write coordination record for any meaningful project change.
Read this file first before any meaningful gameplay, architecture, story or quality decision.
For a new user request: add/update one requirement here, then inspect dependencies/conflicts before implementation.
For a contradiction: preserve both requirements and add/update one decision/open conflict here.
For implementation: update evidence/missing_work/status here only after repository evidence exists.
For testing: update region_quality and active_gate only from actual static/compile/PIE/device/human evidence.
